## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Verijātaka* (Ja 103) is a canonical Jātaka narrative set at Jetavana concerning the wealthy lay disciple Anāthapiṇḍika [Fausböll 1877]. Returning from a village of which he served as headman, Anāthapiṇḍika encountered robbers on the road and chose to press forward through the night into Sāvatthī rather than delay, safely avoiding an attack [Nyanaponika et al. 2003]. Reporting the incident to the Buddha, the Master recounted a parallel story of the past illustrating that the wise have always hastened without delay to escape danger, concluding the tale by identifying the Bodhisatta with the merchant of Bārāṇasī (*Bārāṇasiseṭṭhi*) [Fausböll 1877]. Modern commentators highlight the story in their study of Anāthapiṇḍika to show his realistic prudence in overcoming danger through timely flight rather than displaying false heroism [Nyanaponika et al. 2003].
